newsitem.title: INDIA: India postpones oil price debate for third time.
newsitem.headline: India postpones oil price debate for third time.

text.p: India's ruling United Front coalition has postponed a meeting to consider raising domestic oil prices for the third time but expects to take up the issue next week, an alliance official said on Thursday.
Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's 15-party alliance had been scheduled to meet this Friday to discuss a proposal to raise petroleum prices to help plug a mounting subsidy bill.
"They will be meeting on July 8," the alliance official told Reuters.
Two earlier meetings had already been postponed, mainly because of deep disagreements over how to tackle the subsidy costs.

The government owes state oil companies an estimated 155 billion rupees ($4.3 billion), and the companies have complained they cannot keep importing crude unless domestic prices are raised to bring them more in line with world prices.
Coalition officials said a crisis in Gujral's Janata Dal party, the biggest group in Gujral's 15-party coalition, was the main reason behind the most recent postponement.
The party was holding an election on Thursday to choose a leader, but a faction backing the indicted party chief, Laloo Prasad Yadav, was boycotting the poll.

Yadav, who is chief minister of the eastern state of Bihar, and 55 others have been indicted by federal police in a $280 million corruption case involving the alleged embezzlement of state animal husbandry funds. Yadav says he is innocent.

India's communists are vigorously opposed to any price increase, while Gujral and Finance Minister P. Chidambaram have argued for moderate price rises in some petroleum products coupled with the eventual dismantling of state controls.
The Communist Party of India wants customs and excise duties on oil scrapped and has submitted an alternative plan to avoid higher petroleum prices, which it says would hurt the poor.
Several newspapers have said the United Front, worried that mid-term elections may become inevitable, was growing increasingly reluctant to raise oil prices.
Any increase in petroleum product prices would be the second by the United Front in its one year in power.
Last July the government raised the price of petrol by 25 percent and the prices of high-speed diesel, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) for cooking, paraffin wax and fuel oil by 30 percent.
It was forced to scale back the rise in diesel prices to 15 percent after nationwide protests supported by left-wing parties. ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
